title: feat(mcp): bridge a host-injected authoring ToolRegistry over HTTP behind a metadata:write OAuth scope
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-support-ai"} -->
_Requested by **Yibo Wang** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwB?thread=cmsg_01BVUyyPie8gHwoPM18iABwBQgB4FMqdjyELZJBca9aoRG)_

Fixes #26464

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**:spec 新增 OAuth scope `metadata:write`(连同每个 scope 的授权页文案常量);`@objectstack/mcp` 的 `handleHttpRequest` 接受宿主注入的 authoring ToolRegistry,只对带该 scope 的令牌注册其工具,每次调用都在 tool context 里盖上 `door: 'mcp'` + 令牌主体 + 环境;served SKILL.md 只在有该 scope 时写出这些工具。
- **为什么改**:维护者 2026-10-27 裁决「真审批 + MCP build」:开发者用自己的模型和令牌,经 MCP 在托管环境里构建元数据,落为草稿,人工在界面发布。此前 HTTP 门只有 data/action 工具,令牌连 authoring 都申请不了。
- **风险与回滚**:新增一个 scope 值和一个可选注入口,不注入、不带 scope 时行为逐字节不变;stdio 路径不变。回滚 = revert 本 PR(cloud 消费卡 objectstack-ai/cloud#3302 依赖它,回滚前先停那边)。
- **先看**:`packages/mcp/src/mcp-server-runtime.ts`(`registerAuthoringTools` 的 gate 与 provenance 构造),`packages/mcp/src/mcp-http-tools.ts`(`grantsAuthoringTools`:undefined grant 不放行),`packages/spec/src/ai/mcp.zod.ts`(scope 进 `MCP_OAUTH_SCOPES` ⇒ AS 自动 advertise)。
- **两分钟验证**:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/mcp exec vitest run src/mcp-server-runtime.authoring-scope.test.ts` — 预期 17 条全绿,其中「the refusal is the SAME answer create_record gets without data:write」证明拒绝机制只有一套。
- **需要你做的**:无,席位落地。

## What changes

**`@objectstack/spec` — the scope and its consent copy (`packages/spec/src/ai/mcp.zod.ts`).**

- `MCP_OAUTH_SCOPE_METADATA_WRITE = 'metadata:write'` joins `data:read`, `data:write` and `actions:execute` in `MCP_OAUTH_SCOPES`. Because the authorization server (`@objectstack/plugin-auth`) and the runtime's up-front 403 both read that array, the scope is advertised in `scopes_supported` and admitted by the dispatcher with no further change — the first readers that come for free.
- It is a tool-surface grant, not a data grant: `scopesToAgentPermissionSets` maps it alone to the no-object-access floor, and beside a data scope it changes nothing about the data ceiling (ADR-0090 D10 untouched).
- `MCP_OAUTH_SCOPE_CONSENT_COPY`, keyed by `McpOauthScope`, declares the one consent sentence per scope: the three sentences the Console already renders, verbatim, plus the new one — "Build and change this app's metadata as drafts, within your own permissions — a person publishes them". A scope added without its sentence fails to compile.
- Regenerated `api-surface/ai.json` and `export-origins/ai.json` (two added consts). The authorable surface did not move, hence `Metadata-protocol: none`.

**`@objectstack/mcp` — the first reader (`handleHttpRequest`).**

- `handleHttpRequest(request, { authoring })` takes an optional `McpAuthoringInjection`: the host's `McpAuthoringToolRegistry` plus the token principal (`McpTokenPrincipal`) and the environment. `registerAuthoringTools` registers its tools on the per-request server only when `toolOptions.grantedScopes` names `metadata:write` (`grantsAuthoringTools`, beside the three native family gates in `mcp-http-tools.ts`).
- Without the scope the tools are not registered, so `tools/list` omits them and `tools/call` on one gets the SDK's unknown-tool answer — the same one `create_record` gets without `data:write`, from the same mechanism. The undefined grant of an API key or a session is served no authoring tool: authoring follows the token's consent (see Acceptance notes for the reasoning and the alternative).
- Every call into the registry receives a fresh `McpAuthoringToolContext`: `door: 'mcp'` (`MCP_TOOL_DOOR`), `actor.id` (the principal's user, so a reader that knows only `ToolExecutionContext` runs as that user), `principal` and `environmentId` — built from the host's inputs alone. The inbound `Request` is not in scope of the builder, so no header can reach a tool's context.
- The registration body moved out of the class into a module function with one `execute` seam, so both bridges share it: the stdio `bridgeTools` still calls its registry with one argument (pinned), the HTTP authoring bridge adds the context as the second.
- `renderSkillMarkdown({ grantedScopes, authoringTools })` renders a "Build — authoring tools" section that names the injected tools and teaches the create → verify → draft loop (a person publishes in the UI), and switches the frontmatter description to `OBJECTSTACK_SKILL_DESCRIPTION_WITH_AUTHORING`, only under the same predicate. Every other render is byte-identical to before.
- New exports: `MCP_TOOL_DOOR`, `grantsAuthoringTools`, `OBJECTSTACK_SKILL_DESCRIPTION_WITH_AUTHORING`, and the types `McpToolDoor`, `McpTokenPrincipal`, `McpAuthoringToolContext`, `McpAuthoringToolRegistry`, `McpAuthoringInjection`. `registerAuthoringTools` is exported from its module for the host-less pin, not from the package entry.
- README and `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx` name the fourth scope and what it gates.

The runtime stays door-agnostic: which tools the host injects (cloud ADR-0112 injects no publish or discard tool) and which whitelist version they answer are the host's business. The OSS runtime dispatcher (`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts`) is unchanged and passes no `authoring`; the consumer is objectstack-ai/cloud#3302.

## Why

The card's five numbered changes, on the maintainer's 2026-10-27 ruling (「真审批 + MCP build」, 「同意」): a developer driving an MCP client against a hosted environment could read and run it but never build in it, and no scope existed under which a token could ask for authoring. Triage line 6434128092 grades it p1 `security`: the scope is a boundary, every authoring tool still checks the caller's own metadata permission, landing is drafts-only, and the scope is never a bypass.

## Tests

New pins (all in `packages/mcp` unless noted):

- `mcp-server-runtime.authoring-scope.test.ts` — the gate (a `data:write` token, an `actions:execute` token, an empty grant and the undefined grant can neither list nor call an authoring tool; the registry is never touched), the refusal parity with `create_record` under `data:read` (same shape, same text once the tool name is swapped), the provenance (door, principal, environment, `actor.id`, two-argument call), seven spoofed provenance headers ignored, a fresh context per call, an absent environment absent from the context, the isError and throw paths, and the stdio one-argument pin through a real stdio session.
- `skill-md.authoring.test.ts` — the section renders only for `metadata:write` with at least one tool; every other combination is byte-identical to the default render.
- `skill-md-surface-guard.test.ts` — the drift guard gains the authoring case: the skill rendered for a grant names every tool the surface registers for that grant, and names none of them without the scope.
- `packages/spec/src/ai/mcp-oauth-scopes.test.ts` — the four-scope vocabulary and order, one consent sentence per scope (the three existing ones verbatim), `metadata:write` maps to the floor and changes no data ceiling.

Runs (under `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`, worktree at ``9c3a187a``):

## Acceptance notes

- **Premise.** The card names `docs/adr/0112-cloud-ai-build-lite-boundary.md` and `packages/service-ai-studio/src/authoring-whitelist.ts`; neither exists in this repository (ADR-0112 here is the error-code vocabulary). Both are objectstack-ai/cloud files, cited as cloud ADR-0112; the card's five numbered changes are the build contract, as the claim (6435524505) records.
- **The undefined grant.** For the three native families `grantedScopes: undefined` (API key / session) means "not scope-limited" and keeps the full surface, because each of those calls is bounded by the caller's permissions and RLS. Authoring is registered only for a scope list naming `metadata:write`, so a key or a session is served none. This is the card's literal acceptance ("without the scope it lists none") and the fail-closed reading; widening it to the headless track is a decision for its own card — the predicate carries the reasoning.
- **Refusal shape.** Measured against the pinned SDK (`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.32.1): `tools/call` on an unregistered tool answers a tool error (`result.isError: true`, text naming the tool), not a JSON-RPC error. The parity pin reads either shape and asserts the authoring family gets the same one as `create_record`.
- **Console consent page (out of scope, for the UI lane).** `ui/apps/console/src/pages/auth/OAuthConsentPage.tsx` maps the three agent scopes to sentences in a `switch` and renders any other scope as its raw string, so an OSS consent screen asked for `metadata:write` shows "metadata:write". The sentence now lives in `MCP_OAUTH_SCOPE_CONSENT_COPY` for that page to read. Not changed here: `ui/` is outside this card's file surface.
- **Platform checklist prose.** `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/ai.json` (ai.mcp-http-surface) describes the up-front 403 as "naming all three scopes"; the `WWW-Authenticate` challenge now lists four. The checklist's `--changed-from` judgement is green (anchors intact); the clause wording is for the QA sweep that re-derives it.
- **stdio and the native tools.** No behaviour change: `bridgeTools` keeps its one-argument call (pinned), `wireBridgeTools` and the two native gates are untouched, and the full `@objectstack/mcp` suite is green.

## Verification

Derived gates (`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands`: 104 families; the command set is identical at `9c3a187a` and at the head `cf3ec268`), run in the worktree with every exit code captured before any pipe: 104 run, 104 exit 0 after four environment re-runs, reconciled with `dispatch-gates.mjs --ran` (104 derived, 104 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN).

The four that first answered "nothing measured", and why:

- `check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs --self-test`, exit 3: its fixture is pinned to a commit the shallow clone could not reach. After fetching that commit by its SHA it passes (48 cases).
- `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, exit 3, and `spec check:skill-examples`, exit 3: both read built output the fresh worktree did not have. After a full `pnpm build` (118 tasks successful) both pass (skill-examples: 265 marked examples over 3 surfaces type-check).
- `check:lean-entry-closure`, exit 1: `@objectstack/spec/dist/data/index.mjs` was absent for the seconds in which a sibling spec rebuild had wiped `dist/`. Re-run against the finished build it passes.

Also green, outside the derivation: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated --fix` (14 artifacts up to date; only `api-surface/ai.json` and `export-origins/ai.json` rewritten), `check-platform-checklist --changed-from origin/main` (2 anchored files, 6 anchors judged, 0 lost), `check-nul-bytes` (21342 text files, clean), and eslint with the repo's `--no-inline-config` on the ten changed `.ts` files (0 problems). CI's own families (the artifact roster, the type-check lanes, the path-scheduled jobs) run on this PR; the os-dev report on the card cites them by check-run name and conclusion.
